subject: Post-call: AtlasPay inference economics & pilot asks
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Nair <samir@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: AtlasPay inference economics & pilot asks

Thanks for taking the call earlier, Samir — good to meet you and hear more about AtlasPay's fraud scoring and chat automations. Quick recap from our side and suggested next steps to keep momentum.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Token/unit cost is the single biggest line item for the fraud scoring pipeline (batch scoring + on-demand scoring for appeals).
- Current infra (self-hosted Triton on p3dn-like instances) has spiky usage and unpredictable preemption/maintenance windows that cause misspent GPU minutes.
- You want predictable cost and consistent p95 latency for the user-facing workflows (fraud alerts and chat fallback).

Current stack & constraints you described:
- Model: mix of finetuned open LLMs for chat + smaller distilled models for scoring; some HTTP-backed feature enrichment service.
- Serving: in-house Triton + autoscaling groups; session state kept in Redis KV; persistent keys for user histories.
- Monthly volume: ~180M tokens (infer) today with heavy tail during peak hours; expected ~2.5x growth in 9–12 months.

Success criteria you gave (captured):
- Unit economics: target at least 35–45% reduction in $/1K tokens versus current baseline to justify switching.
- Latency: p95 generation < 250ms for chat paths, p95 scoring < 200ms for small-model hot paths.
- Reliability: grace under degraded capacity (automated fallback to smaller quantized variant).

Key technical preferences & openness:
- Open to 4-bit/quantized variants for the scoring path if quality delta is acceptable.
- Expectation for prefix/KV caching for repeated context (especially appeals flows).
- Willing to run a 6–8 week pilot with representative traffic (we discussed synthetic vs. sampled production traffic).

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) I attached a starter cost-model (atlaspay-cost-model.xlsx) — please fill in current hourly GPU rates and any internal infra costs you want us to include.
2) Aditya will propose a pilot SOW that maps to the success criteria above and includes quantization/latency gates.
3) We ask for a 24–48 hour sample of tokenized request distribution (or a synthetic profile) so we can size batching and prefix-cache expectations. Link for transfer: https://drive.redwood.com/AtlasPay/pilot_data_profile.csv
4) Scheduling: propose kickoff next Monday (2026-02-16) for a 30–45 minute technical kickoff to lock down data/instrumentation.

If this looks right, please reply with: (A) who on your side will own the pilot, (B) whether you can provide a 24–48h sample, and (C) any hard constraints on contract start/end dates.

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments referenced: atlaspay-cost-model.xlsx (attached)
From: Samir Nair <samir@atlaspay.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: AtlasPay inference economics & pilot asks

Thanks, Evelyn — this is perfect and captures the discussion. Quick answers inline:

A) Pilot owner: I'll own it on the AtlasPay side; looping in Priya (legal) and Mateo (infra) after this note.
B) Data sample: we can provide a 48-hour tokenized profile and a 48-hour aggregated traffic histogram (non-PII). We'll push the files to the Drive link by Friday 2026-02-13.
C) Timing: procurement window is end of Q2; pilot needs to complete by mid-May to feed into the budget. If Redwood can show the unit economics delta within 6 weeks we can accelerate.

A few clarifications from our engineers: 
- Our current "scoring" path is ~150ms median and ~320ms p95 on GPU, but it blows up under contention; we'd like to get p95 under 200ms consistently.
- We have a hard SLO for the chat FAST path of p95 < 250ms — can't compromise here.
- On quantization: open to 4-bit for scoring if degradation is <2% AUC drop; chat is more sensitive.

Also: I wasn't clear on how Redwood handles prefix caching for session histories — is that automatic or requires custom instrumentation?

I'll confirm the Drive upload and the pilot owner list (Priya/Mateo) in a follow-up.

—Samir
Head of Product, AtlasPay
samir@atlaspay.com

Subject: Fwd: Post-call: AtlasPay inference economics & pilot asks

Samir — quick technical follow-up from our infra team. I'm forwarding a proposed pilot scope (attached as pilot-sow.pdf) and a lightweight checklist. Main asks below.

Summary of pilot scope (high-level):
- Duration: 6 weeks (2w ramp, 3w evaluation, 1w stabilization).
- Goals: demonstrate >=35% unit-cost savings at matched quality on scoring path; p95 latencies within your SLOs; transparent cost breakdown.
- Approach: run parallel inference flows (AtlasPay traffic mirrored to Redwood sandbox) using quantized and full-precision variants, with real-time tracing and token-level cost accounting.

Technical asks from AtlasPay to support sizing and configuration: 
1) Sample payloads (anonymized) and tokenization rules so we can estimate average tokens per request.
2) Traffic profile by hour and by endpoint (scoring vs chat). We need to size batching windows and expected concurrency.
3) Any redlines on data residency or encryption (KMS/HSM) for the sandbox.

Notes on caching/batching: 
- Redwood's runtime supports prefix/KV caching out of the box; we will show expected hit rates from your sample and recommend cache TTLs.
- Continuous batching can be tuned to hit throughput targets while meeting p95 latency; we'll provide config knobs in the pilot SOW.

We attached pilot-sow.pdf and the cost workbook; please have your infra/data person reply with the sample files and an owner for the Drive upload. Happy to have a short tech sync Friday (2026-02-13) if that helps.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
